definitions.explanation: A line made of long dashes alternating with single dots (— · — ·), used in technical drawings for centerlines, lines of symmetry, and boundaries. A term from drafting and school technical-drawing classes.

examples.japanese: {中心線|ちゅうしんせん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{一点鎖線|いってんさせん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{描|か}く→描く：28436_kaku⟧。
examples.english: Centerlines are drawn as dash-dot lines.

examples.japanese: ⟦{図面|ずめん}→図面：12023_zumen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{一点鎖線|いってんさせん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{対称|たいしょう}→対称：31144_taishou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{軸|じく}→軸：14304_jiku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{示|しめ}している→示す：01948_shimesu⟧。
examples.english: The dash-dot line on the drawing marks the axis of symmetry.

examples.japanese: {製図|せいず}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{授業|じゅぎょう}→授業：00781_jugyou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦{実線|じっせん}→実線：20763_jissen⟧、⟦{破線|はせん}→破線：20764_hasen⟧、{一点鎖線|いってんさせん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{使|つか}い{分|わ}け→使い分け：11559_tsukaiwake⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{習|なら}った→習う：00479_narau⟧。
examples.english: In drafting class, we learned when to use solid lines, dashed lines, and dash-dot lines.

notes:
From ⟦{一点|いってん}→一点：08894_itten⟧ (one dot) and {鎖線|させん} (chain line, a line of dashes broken by dots). The standard line types in Japanese technical drawing are named by what they look like.

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{実線|じっせん}→実線：20763_jissen⟧: solid line (visible outlines)
- ⟦{破線|はせん}→破線：20764_hasen⟧: dashed line (hidden edges)
- ⟦{点線|てんせん}→点線：18308_tensen⟧: dotted line
- {二点鎖線|にてんさせん}: dash-double-dot line (imaginary or alternate positions)
- {一点鎖線|いってんさせん}: dash-dot line (centerlines, symmetry axes, boundaries)
